about: The path-to-checks map (Q65, 2026-09-29; its minimum semantics Q65a, the reviewer's ruling in docs/review/responses/198c148.md), read by tools/docs/checks_for_paths.py for the orchestrator's chain. For each path a seam touches it names the smallest set of checks that can tell the mechanisms the path reaches apart from their alternatives, plus the cheap universal guards where they apply: typecheck, lint, the unit suite and the app build for app code; the content build, the validator and the record check where content or the pipeline changes. A browser spec is named because docs/08's file lines or a landing chain tie it to the path's module; the whole default Playwright configuration is named only where a module's behaviour runs on every spec's path (the entry and boot, the shell, the router, the global style, the build and test configuration, the Playwright harness), so no named list bounds it, and each such reason says what the module reaches. The full unit and Playwright suites are merged-tree CI's and the fallback's: a path no pattern names takes the full required suites and is printed as unmatched. The owner's rule of 2026-09-27 (the full browser suite for the engine, the session and Today, the schema, the router and shell, the renderer) is CI's, not the map's. Judgement may always add checks for cross-cutting risk; the map never subtracts one. Every pattern matching a path contributes (the union). tools/content/tests/test_ci_order.py asserts CI runs every check below that carries a ci step; tools/content/tests/test_checks_for_paths.py asserts every named file exists, every pattern matches a path, a test-side helper's list names every file that reads it, and the two screen frames name the union of the specs their importing screens' rows give.
